question: Your support agent handles a customer who reports a locked account and a duplicate $89 charge. The agent unlocks the account, confirms the duplicate with lookup_order, and calls escalate_to_human because disputed charges need human approval. The handoff contains the customer ID and the note "Billing dispute, see the conversation above; please resolve." Human agents work from a queue without transcript access, and they re-ask customers for details and sometimes refund the wrong charge. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The agent unlocked the account before it escalated, instead of handing the whole request to a human agent, so the case was split between two owners.
options.reason: The guide supports decomposing multi-concern requests into distinct items and resolving them, so the unlock is not why human agents re-ask for the billing details.

options.text: The agent escalated the duplicate charge instead of calling process_refund itself, so human agents now receive cases that the agent should have closed on first contact.
options.reason: Disputed charges need human approval here, so escalation is correct; the problem is what the handoff contains, not the decision to escalate.

options.text: The note relies on a transcript that the human agent cannot see, instead of stating the root cause, refund amount and recommended action.
options.reason: The guide says that escalations to humans who lack the transcript need a compiled structured summary with customer ID, root cause, refund amount and recommended action.

options.text: The note uses neutral wording instead of quoting the customer's own messages, so the human agent cannot judge the urgency of the dispute.
options.reason: Quoted customer messages are not a structured summary and still lack the root cause, refund amount and recommended action that the human agent needs.
